text.p: Petro-Canada said on Wednesday it agreed to swap its interests in the Golden Lake heavy oil property in Saskatchewan for cash plus natural gas properties owned by PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd.

Petro-Canada said it would boost its interests in the Benjamin Creek field and acquire interests in the Limestone field in southwestern Alberta, adding natural gas production of about 13 million cubic feet per day.
It would also receive C$22.5 million in cash.
In exchange, PanCanadian would receive all of Petro-Canada's interests in the Golden Lake area in west-central Saskatchewan. Current production from the region is about 2,250 barrels per day.

"This asset swap is another step in our strategy to expand our Western Canada natural gas reserves and production capability," Petro-Canada executive vice-president Norm McIntyre said in a statement. "The new properties, which are within our core areas of operation, also have further development potential."
The transaction, which wouldl be effective June 1, 1996, is subject to due diligence and regulatory approvals.
Closing is expected to take place later this year, Petro-Canada said.
